recipes.title: Chicken Parmesan
recipes.notes: Sauce is better made the day before. Half quantities fit one pan; doubling means frying in batches or the crust steams.

steps.text: Butterfly the cutlets and pound them to an even 1 cm. Season both sides and leave them out while you set up the breading.
Set out three dishes: flour, beaten eggs, and panko mixed with half the parmesan.
Bread the cutlets: flour, egg, then the panko and parmesan mix. Press the crumbs on firmly.
Simmer the tomatoes with the onion and a glug of oil for 20 minutes, until it thickens. Season and set aside.
Fry in a shallow pan over medium-high heat, three minutes a side, until deep golden. Drain on a rack, not paper.
Spoon sauce over each cutlet, top with torn mozzarella and the rest of the parmesan, and grill until blistered. Finish with basil.
Stir everything together in a jar, seal it, and leave it in the fridge overnight.
Loosen with a splash more milk in the morning.
Brown the chicken in the oil, then lift it out.
Soften the onion, carrot and potato in the same pot for ten minutes.
Return the chicken, add the water, and simmer until the vegetables give.
Off the heat, melt the roux blocks in and simmer five more minutes until it coats a spoon.
Pat the fillets dry, rub with oil and paprika, and season.
Air fry at 200Ã‚Â°C for nine minutes, skin down, until it flakes.
Cook the rice and let it cool to room temperature.
Dice the tuna, avocado and cucumber into even cubes.
Whisk the dressing, fold it through the tuna, and build the bowls.
Soften the onion in the oil, then toast the cumin for a minute.
Add the chickpeas, tomatoes and coconut milk and simmer fifteen minutes.
Wilt the spinach through at the end and season hard.

Whisk the eggs and sugar until pale, then fold in the chocolate.
